title: He Sold the Eiffel Tower… Twice 🗼 #shorts
hook: He sold the Eiffel Tower. Twice.
cast: a sly thin con man with a thin black moustache, grey 1920s three-piece suit and a black bowler hat

lines.say: In 1925, a man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back and tried to sell it again.
shots: {hero} grinning and holding a giant SOLD sign in front of the Eiffel Tower, Paris street, golden hour
close-up of {hero} winking at the camera, Eiffel Tower blurred behind

lines.say: His name was Victor Lustig, and he read in a newspaper that the tower was rusting and cost a fortune to repair.
shots: {hero} reading a big newspaper at a small Paris cafe table, steam rising from a coffee cup
the Eiffel Tower covered in orange rust patches, workers on ropes painting it, grey sky

lines.say: So he faked government papers, and invited six scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting in a fancy hotel.
shots: {hero} stamping official looking papers with a big rubber stamp at a desk, candle light
six chubby businessmen in suits around a long table in a luxurious hotel room, chandelier, secretive mood

lines.say: He told them the city would tear the tower down, and sell all that iron to one lucky buyer. Shh, keep it secret.
shots: {hero} leaning over the table whispering with a finger on his lips, businessmen leaning in
miniature Eiffel Tower being dismantled by a crane, piles of iron beams, dramatic sky

lines.say: A dealer named Andre Poisson believed every word, and paid him a huge bribe on top.
shots: a nervous chubby businessman handing over a briefcase overflowing with banknotes, hotel corridor
{hero} counting a thick stack of cash with a big smile

lines.say: Lustig jumped on a train to Vienna with the money. And Poisson? He was too embarrassed to tell the police.
shots: a steam train speeding out of a station at night, {hero} waving from the window
the chubby businessman blushing bright red, hiding his face behind a newspaper

lines.say: So a month later, Lustig came back, and tried the same trick again.
shots: {hero} stepping off a train with a suitcase, Paris skyline and Eiffel Tower behind, morning
{hero} again at a hotel table with a new group of businessmen

lines.say: This time the buyer went to the police. Lustig escaped. Would you have bought the tower?
shots: french police officers with whistles running down a cobblestone street at night
{hero} tipping his bowler hat and walking away under the Eiffel Tower at night, moonlight

description:
In 1925 con man Victor Lustig 'sold' the Eiffel Tower to a scrap dealer, then came back and tried to do it again. A true story.

Sources: Smithsonian Magazine; Wikipedia: Victor Lustig.

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
